timing: retrospective specification of previously generated candidate

sourceFacts.fact: Developmental delay concerns later acquisition of expected skills.
Regression is loss of a previously acquired skill and is distinguished by the child's prior abilities.

clinicalSources.title: CDC: Social and language regression study

invariants: Upper row gains word; lower row loses prior word.
Empty bubble is a single skill example, not absence of all communication.
expectedLabels: Delay or loss of a skill?
A previously acquired skill is lost
Ask what the child could do before
layoutSpecification: Two rows of a simple conceptual skill trajectory with warm hand-painted child motif, no medical device. Title 'Delay or loss of a skill?'. Upper row heading 'Delay': three small speech bubbles progressing left to right from empty, empty, to the word 'ball'; small time arrow below; sentence 'A skill is acquired later'. Lower row 'Regression': three small speech bubbles from 'ball', 'ball', to empty fading outline; sentence 'A previously acquired skill is lost'. Use same neutral child icon beside each row; no distressed face. Bottom 'Ask what the child could do before'. No ages, test scores, normal-range claim, autism label or predicted outcome. The empty bubble means example of absent word, not inability to communicate by other means.
forbiddenAnatomy: No claimed anatomical reconstruction, diagnostic image, histology or literal neuroanatomical pathway
No organ cutaways or invented internal spatial relationships

validation.pixelChecks: Visually inspected: upper sequence acquires the example word later, lower sequence loses a previously shown word; headings, time arrows and captions agree. No ages, diagnosis, outcome prediction or claim about all communication ability.
